subject: degree freedom of binary item measurement invariance

messages.author: c242febbf5e3a49a
messages.subject: degree freedom of binary item measurement invariance
parts:
Hi everyone, I conducted a measurement invariance test for a binary scale. I treat them as ordinal data and use wlsmv as estimator.  I found when the degree of freedom of the model with constraining loading, threshold, and intercepts is smaller than the model with constraining loading and threshold. Could the reason be the binary item?

The package is Lavaan 0.6 - 9, semTools 0.5-5.

Thank you,
Hao

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: degree freedom of binary item measurement invariance
parts:
I assume you are testing invariance across groups?  Constraining intercepts will free the latent mean in all but one group, thus lowering your df.  You don't gain any df because either the intercepts are already fixed to zero (default in lavaan) or if you are using measEq.syntax() with the defaults, then constraining an intercept will release the constraint on the same item's residual variance.
